text:
alanna: Heads-up — I pushed a prototype card to the cost dashboard that slices cost by route -> model -> cache-savings. want quick feedback before i surface it org-wide :eyes:

alanna: Main question: do we show ‘amortized GPU cost after cache credits’ as the default or keep gross GPU cost and show credits as a separate column?

kevin: I vote for defaulting to net (after credits). most product teams expect bill-like numbers. show gross in a collapsible detail :thumbsup:

morgan: net is good, but watch out for double-counting when requests get rerouted. if route A gets cache credit but later falls back to route B, credits might be applied at the original route level and again at aggregated tenant-level if we’re not careful.

ryan: +1 on morgan. we need a single canonical attribution step. propose adding a `cache_credit_owner` field in telemetry: values {route, tenant, model_variant}. then UI can choose attribution policy.

alanna: @ryan what would that look like in our events? simple flag or need lineage?

ryan: minimal viable: `cache_credit_owner` + `cache_hit_origin` (e.g. kv-cache, prefix-cache, shared-tenant-cache). lineage later if we need per-prefix mapping.

kevin: also add an opt-in sampling toggle on the dashboard query. per-request join to cache tables is expensive for historical ranges. default to 1% sample with extrapolation, but allow full-query for 7d windows.

alanna: good call. UX thought: show small badge "sampled" with the sample rate and CI bar if sampling used.

morgan: on visualization: for unit economics drilldown — do stacked bars (gpu cost / cache credits / infra overhead) or sparkline + tooltip with breakdown? I think stacked bars for month-over-month, sparkline for quick route list.

kevin: stacked bars give immediate sense of savings. sparklines for route list to keep rows compact. combo is fine.

devx-bot: FYI here's a cheap-ish sql pattern we used for chargeback previews earlier. can adapt to include `cache_credit_owner`:

```
SELECT
  route_id,
  model_sku,
  count(*) as requests,
  sum(gpu_token_cost) as gross_gpu_cost,
  sum(case when cache_hit then gpu_token_cost * cache_credit_rate else 0 end) as cache_credits
FROM
  inference_events
LEFT JOIN cache_events USING(request_id)
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY route_id, model_sku;
```

ops-chris: We should gate the full per-request view behind an experimental flag and warn customers about potential bill diffs. we caused confusion last time when granular credits appeared in console that didn't match billing exports. :grimacing:

alanna: Agreed. rollout plan: feature-flag + internal-only preview for a week, then opt-in beta for top 10 tenants, then global.

kevin: small nit — include routing policy column (sticky routing, latency_fallback, cost_fallback) so users can filter routes that rely on fallback tiers. helps explain weird cost spikes.

morgan: also add a column for `cache_reuse_rate` (percent) and `median_kv_ttl` so teams can understand whether caching improvements will move needle.

ryan: can we also expose a `model_instance_hours` amortized field? some customers ask in terms of GPU-hours not tokens.

alanna: yes, will add `amortized_gpu_hours` derived from token-rate profile. will need infra input for vCPU/GPU blends.

alanna: next actions: i’ll wire up `cache_credit_owner` to telemetry schema PR, add sampling toggle on dashboard prototype, and mock stacked bar + sparkline combo. tagging @kevin @morgan @ryan for review when PRs land. thanks! :raised_hands:
